That Math.max is a one-sided guard pointing the wrong way (HAZARDS 0b): when three facts are wide enough that the even spread falls under 10 units, the max RESTORES 10 and pushes the last fact back off the right edge — reintroducing the clip at wider data. It also landed the three-fact case with its right edge at exactly W, on the clip boundary. factLayout() clamps on one side only, reserves 2 units, floors the gap at 6, and — this is the point — leaves right > W TRUE rather than clamping it away, so meta.facts_fit can be false and R2 can fail.

arbitration_questions.question: RI-UIX03 C7 requires the full description unabbreviated and untruncated. RI-UIX09 DN5 requires the detail panel to lead with a depiction, and DN4 requires D2 >= 0.15. Measured over all 45 carried records, the container band satisfies C7 at 45 of 45 ONLY with the depiction deleted (plate 0), and shrinking the plate to 90 to reach 41 of 45 puts D2 near 0.148, under the floor. Which yields?
arbitration_questions.what_i_did_not_do: I did not weaken either row and I did not pretend to satisfy C7. The build takes every line the room genuinely holds (2 -> 4) and publishes description_lines_shown / description_lines_needed so the shortfall is readable off getUIState() on any item without re-deriving the wrap.
arbitration_questions.the_shape_of_an_answer_i_would_expect: Either the band is not the only place a description may live (a press-to-read expansion is a Morrowind affordance and costs no panel area at rest), or C7 is scoped to a surface that can hold it. Both are rulings, neither is a build.

arbitration_questions.question: S61 makes the band fail-closed and requires it measured per screen. Measured here, band_perturb and band_mode are 0.0000 on every screen and the entire band is band_ref — the per-capture re-derivation of the modal colour. If the reference were pinned to the declared ground colour from getUIState().materials, the band would collapse to the threshold sweep alone. Should the band be measured against a moving reference at all, when the movement is a property of the INSTRUMENT rather than of the build?
arbitration_questions.note: Asked against my own interest: the band I published is the largest of the four arms and it is the one my container has to clear.

hazards_worth_adding.shape: A CHECK THAT READS A DECLARATION CANNOT SEE A DRAW, AND IT WILL REPORT GREEN.
hazards_worth_adding.instances_in_this_thread_alone: round 4/5's gold column declared a value the clip removed entirely; round 6's weight column declared '11.5' and drew '11…'; round 6's condition fact was declared and clipped away whole; round 7's own R1 split the declared text and reported 0 truncations; round 7's own R2 was a literal true.
hazards_worth_adding.the_general_form: This is HAZARDS 22 in the UI: 22 is 'your baseline was never loaded', this is 'your assertion was never rendered'. The fix in both cases is the same and costs one field — make the thing under test PUBLISH what it actually did, and read that. chrome.js row() and inventory.js factLayout() are the two examples; both derive once and are consumed by the draw, so the published number and the drawn glyph cannot disagree by construction.
hazards_worth_adding.the_tell: If a check would return the same answer against a build with the drawing code deleted, it is reading a declaration.
